## TL;DR

Inventoried every keyboard shortcut the web UI ships, then headless-tested the
command palette and the board navigation against fixtures. Found and fixed four
real defects: Escape leaked out of the palette into every window-level handler
behind it (one Esc over an open task drawer closed both), the palette could lose
the z-index tie against an open drawer, a `:focus-visible` rule referenced a
custom property that was never defined (three dead focus rings), and the
palette's close button had no visible focus indicator at all. Two regression
suites (26 jsdom tests + 4 WebKit fixture audits at 375/768/1280) and a QA doc
lock it all down.

## Work and rationale

**Inventory first.** I mapped every window/document keydown listener in
`src/ui-app/src`: ⌘K/Ctrl+K palette (SearchBar, with repo/settings delegating to
scoped palettes), the palette's own ↑↓/Enter/Esc/Tab trap, the opt-in board
navigation (j/k/h/l/arrows/Enter/two-stage Esc), settings roving tabs,
Enter-to-send composers, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter form submits, and the Radix drawer's Esc
path. Touch behavior was already right (#1139/#1152): kbd chips and the palette
legend hide on `hover: none`/`pointer: coarse`, the pill becomes a 44×44 icon
button at phone width, and the mobile bar's Search tab opens the palette without
a keyboard. Discoverability is covered by the header chip, the scoped palettes'
chips, the palette footer legend, and the Settings row documenting the board keys
— I verified those rather than adding yet another list.

**The Esc leak was the important find.** radix-vue's drawer honors
`defaultPrevented` on Escape, so I initially expected the layering to be fine —
but the board-nav composable (and HotfixConfirmDialog, DiffView's back
navigation, the deployments confirm, ChatQueuedNotice, MobileTabs' sheet) listen
at window level and don't check it. Fixing at the consumer side would have meant
touching six handlers; fixing at the source — the palette is the topmost layer
while open, so an Esc it handles is *its* Esc — is one `stopPropagation()` in
`SearchOverlay.onKey`, exactly the pattern AreaPicker already uses. I then wrote
the integration test against the real composable: Esc with the palette over an
open drawer closes only the palette; the next Esc closes the drawer; with the
palette closed the two-stage Esc is byte-for-byte the old behavior.

**The z-index tie** (`palette 100 == drawer 100`) I found by walking the
stylesheet's layer ladder; the palette now sits at 160 — above drawers (100),
jump-to-latest (130) and the shot viewer (140/150), below tooltip (200) and card
preview (300) — with a comment documenting the ladder, and a test asserting the
ordering by parsing the CSS.

**The dead focus rings** surfaced because my WebKit test asserting the close
button's `:focus-visible` outline kept failing: `.search-overlay-close` had no
ring rule, and while fixing that I noticed three rules using
`var(--focus-ring)` — a variable defined nowhere, so invalid-at-computed-value
time paints nothing. All now use the real `--ring` token, plus a table-driven
guard that fails if any outline declaration references an undefined custom
property (the whole class, not just the one instance).

## Approaches tried

For the WebKit evidence I reused the repo's established split: mount the real
components in jsdom (seeded store + typed query), serialize the rendered markup,
inject it with the real stylesheet, and audit overflow/visibility at the three
QA widths. My first attempt walked Tab to the close button in WebKit; that fails
for a platform reason — macOS WebKit skips buttons on Tab unless Full Keyboard
Access is on — so the Tab-trap assertion moved to jsdom against the real
component and the WebKit test asserts the focus ring the way
`dialog-overlay-browser.test.ts` does (explicit focus + `:focus-visible`).

## Challenges and blockers

- Bare `bunx vitest` doesn't load the Vue plugin; tests must run through
  `bun run test:vitest`. Minor, but cost one false start.
- jsdom lacks `scrollIntoView`; the board nav calls it on every move. Stubbed in
  the suite.
- The scoped `repoos check` first failed on a `Ref<boolean>` typing nit in the
  harness (the gate runs vue-tsc over tests too — good), and had to be re-run
  after fixing. One warning about a skipped WIP checkpoint is expected while a
  check is running.

## Key learnings

- When a floating layer consumes a key, consume it completely: `preventDefault`
  alone stops the default action but not sibling window-level listeners that
  implement the same key elsewhere. The repo already knew this (AreaPicker's
  `stopPropagation`, StopWorkConfirmModal's open-stack guard); the palette was
  the odd one out.
- CSS custom properties fail silently: `outline: 2px solid var(--undefined)`
  computes to no outline at all. A grep-level guard is cheap insurance.
- Platform behavior differs where you least expect it: headless WebKit tabbing
  to buttons is off by default on macOS. Test the app's trap logic in jsdom,
  keep browser fixtures to layout/visual evidence.

## Verification

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes (build, typecheck, lint, CSS
guards, rendered contrast, scoped tests, WebKit smoke). New suites:
`keyboard-shortcuts-qa.test.ts` (26 jsdom tests), `keyboard-shortcuts-qa-browser.test.ts`
(4 WebKit fixture audits). QA write-up: `docs/qa/2026-11-keyboard-shortcuts-qa.md`.
No `repoos.toml` change; no runtime dependency; `dist/` untouched.
